summary: 11 requirements (6 functional, 5 non-functional); 20 ambiguities resolved as assumptions, 0 unresolved.
decisions: What short-code length and alphabet should generated codes use?: Use 8-character generated codes from [A-Za-z0-9_-], case-sensitive. Regenerate a code if it collides with an active code, tombstone, or service route. (assumption)
What redirect status code should the service return (301 vs 302)?: Return 302 Found and include Cache-Control: no-store. (assumption)
What should happen when a custom alias is already taken?: Return HTTP 409 Conflict for an alias assigned to either an active link or a tombstone. (assumption)

What HTTP paths, payload fields, and successful response bodies should the v1 API use?: Use POST /api/links with JSON fields `url`, optional `alias`, and optional `expiresAt`; return 201 with `code`, `shortPath`, and `managementToken`. Use GET /{code} for redirects, GET /api/links/{code} for metadata, DELETE /api/links/{code} for deletion, and GET /health for health. Metadata fields are `originalUrl`, `createdAt`, and `expiresAt`. (assumption)

What format should expiry use, and how should an expiry at or before creation time be handled?: Use an ISO-8601 UTC instant in the `expiresAt` field, normalize returned timestamps to UTC, and reject an expiry at or before creation time with HTTP 400. (assumption)

What response behavior should apply to unknown, deleted, expired, malformed, and unauthorized requests?: Return HTTP 400 for malformed or invalid create input, 409 for a taken alias, 429 with Retry-After when rate-limited, 302 for an active redirect, 410 for an expired redirect, and 404 for an unknown or deleted code. Metadata for an expired non-deleted link returns 200; metadata for an unknown or deleted code returns 404. On deletion, return 401 for a missing token, 403 for an invalid token, 204 on success, and 404 for an unknown or deleted code. (assumption)

Should the create response contain an absolute short URL, and how is its public origin determined?: Return the relative `shortPath` and code, not an absolute URL; clients combine the path with the service origin they already use. (assumption)

How should the management token be generated, exposed, and validated?: Generate a cryptographically random 256-bit token, encode it as unpadded base64url, return it only in the creation response, and store a SHA-256 hash. Accept it in X-Management-Token and keep it valid until successful deletion; do not persist or log the plaintext token. (assumption)

What should happen if DNS resolution fails or returns both allowed and prohibited addresses during URL validation?: Fail closed: reject the URL if resolution fails, times out, yields no usable address, or any returned address is prohibited. (assumption)

How should the service identify a client IP when requests may include forwarding headers?: Use the network peer address by default and do not trust forwarding headers unless a trusted-proxy configuration is explicitly provided. (assumption)
What does the health endpoint check?: Return HTTP 200 with an UP status when the service and H2 store are available; return HTTP 503 otherwise. (assumption)

What qualifies as meaningful automated test coverage?: Tests must exercise every functional requirement and the important validation, authorization, expiry, rate-limit, persistence, and redirect failure paths; no numeric coverage percentage is required. (assumption)

How many requests should the latency test use for warm-up, and should measured requests be concurrent?: Use 1,000 sequential warm-up requests followed by the 1,000 measured requests from a single client. (assumption)
